description: Hard-risk EDGE golden (PLATFORM_CONVENTIONS.md section 11): the branches the single-engine script of expected_risk_decisions.json cannot reach. Generated by python/tools/make_golden_risk_edge.py from the Python reference-equivalent port; replayed by Rust, Java and Python. `scenarios` are independent: each builds a fresh engine from `config` (minus the [section, key] named by `config_remove`, when present; then every [section, key, value] of `config_set` assigned, when present) and the `instruments` table, calls require_bootstrap when `require_bootstrap` is true, then runs `steps`. Step types are those of expected_risk_decisions.json plus: bad_kill / bad_unkill (a kill command whose scope_id does not parse: the call must fail), bootstrap (bootstrap_positions with `fills`), restore (snapshot the engine and continue on the engine restored from that snapshot, continuing its audit chain; the audit of the engine before the restore is kept), and since x-version 2: trade (on_market_trade), cancel_request (on_cancel_request) and bad_override (an override_loss_limit call that must fail). expected_risk_edge_audit.jsonl is the audit JSONL of every scenario in order (across a restore: the old engine's log, then the restored engine's) and must be reproduced byte for byte. `must_pin` lists [rule_id, reason fragment] pairs that must each match at least one audit line.
